newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stocks end off as interest wanes.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stocks end off as interest wanes.

text.p: Caracas stocks closed off in thin trade on waning interest in Venezuelan equities, traders and analysts said.
"The majority of both local and international investors are in a selling mode," said Intervalores broker Ricardo Marino.
The bourse's 19-share index closed down 1.07 percent at 6,253.59 points as 14 million shares exchanged hands, worth 1.2 billion bolivars ($2.5 million).
"Everyone's looking much more closely at New York, leaving them rather neglectful down here," he added.
Many analysts had expected a surging bolsa after Venezuela reached a ground-breaking agreement to reform its crumbling social security system late last month.

"Venezuela is (now) a more attractive country in which to invest, but there aren't really that many attractive stocks to buy on the stock market -- today," wrote InvestAnalysis consultant Alex Dalamady in a recent research note.
Merinvest's composite index, which includes telephone company CANTV, ended down 0.92 percent at 95.10 points.
